_comment: The SHORT format: two pools of three, then a four-team
double-elimination playoff. This file now holds MORE THAN ONE of
them -- `seasons` is a list, oldest first, and `current` names the
UNLIKE data/fixtures.json this file is HAND-AUTHORED. It is an input,
not an output: only the parts that cannot be worked out are written
down. The pool matches, the playoff boxes, who feeds which box, the
tie-break fixtures, the final placings and every count on the page
are DERIVED by export_web.build_mini() -- so a pool edited here
redraws the whole page and no two numbers can disagree.
A season either names its own teams inline (`teams`) or leaves it out
and resolves ids against data/teams.json. Season 1 does the latter,
because it was played by the league's registered teams. Season 2 does
the former: its six teams are new, they are not on any roster in
teams.json, and a team named here can never claim a league result --
which is exactly what keeps it safe to name them here.
Team ids are SCOPED TO A SEASON. Season 2's team 1 is not Season 1's
team 1. Nothing crosses between seasons: results, tie-breaks and
standings all live inside their own season object.

seasons.name: Season 1
seasons.note: Played by the league's registered teams, so its ids resolve against data/teams.json.

provisional_teams.name: narai_co
provisional_teams.note: On the captains' sheet only -- two players named, three chairs empty.

_results_note: REPORTED results -- a winner and nothing else, told to the bot
rather than read off a scoreboard. Everywhere else in this project
a result arrives as a screenshot and is checksummed before it
counts. Give a result a "source_ref" naming a game in
data/league_matches.json and the page stops flagging it.
A pairing can occur TWICE -- once in the group, once in the replay
-- and one result was filed against the wrong one for two days.
Always establish which stage a reported result belongs to.
tie_breaks: The result between the two teams
If that settles nothing, the tied teams replay it — a single-game round robin between just them

seasons.name: Season 2
seasons.note: Seven teams: a pool of three and a pool of four, two advancing from each. CPX's Return withdrew on 2026-08-26 and Beast_Yona_Co took its slot and id. Team Seeker and Team Chainskooter were added on 2026-08-27, one drawn into each pool; Chainskooter withdrew on 2026-08-28 before playing a game, leaving Pool A with three. Two of three advance in Pool A against two of four in Pool B -- an uneven shot at the bracket, and the price of running seven teams in a format built for even pools.
_draw: The pools were DRAWN, not chosen, and both draws are reproducible:
-> [5, 6, 2, 1, 3, 4]   first three = Pool A, last three = Pool B
-> [8, 7]   first = Pool A, second = Pool B
Team Chainskooter (8) withdrew on 2026-08-28 before playing, which is
why Pool A is the short one -- that is where the draw had put them,
not a choice. Pool A therefore plays a three-team round robin and
Pool B a four-team one; two still advance from each.
A draw nobody can re-run is indistinguishable from one that was
arranged. Re-run those two lines to check this one.
